A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same HumorDB paper and complete supplementary Sections 7–13. All 17 pages were compared through text extraction and rendering; the material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original human humor judgments, model evaluations on three tasks, explanation and attention analyses, and supplementary in-lab validation.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original human-study results, model evaluations, and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: Dataset construction, model heads, prompts, fine-tuning procedures, attention analysis, and layerwise logit attribution are unchanged in the main text and appendices.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same HumorDB image categories and three humor tasks, the 650-image MSCOCO/Places365 control set, and the 400-image in-lab validation.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in every corresponding experiment, including the vision models, LLaVA and BLIP variants, GPT-4o, Gemini-Flash, and human and chance comparisons.

E3.justification: Data splits, participant screening, evaluation metrics, prompts, model configurations, and training settings match. Appendix 7.1 retains the same 10-epoch budget and validation-based checkpoint selection.

E4.justification: The editing-artifact controls, original-only comparisons, explanation case studies, attention-map and layerwise analyses, and annotation-validation study are retained without revision.

E5.justification: Appendix 7.1 specifies the same five runs for models other than GPT-4o and Gemini-Flash, which receive one run. Standard-deviation and human-reliability reporting are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted findings, and qualitative model responses match. For example, Table 3 retains RMSEs of 1.68 and 1.66 for LLaVA fine-tuned with words on testAllSet and testOnlyPairs, respectively.

T1.justification: The metric definitions and mathematical descriptions of attention and layerwise analysis are identical. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: HumorDB, minimally contrastive image pairs, human evaluation across three tasks, and evidence of limitations in AI humor understanding.

C2.justification: The discussion retains identical interpretations of contrastive-pair failures, attention and explanation limitations, and possible training-data familiarity, together with the same dataset-size and cultural/demographic limitations.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility disclosures match, including optimizer settings, hyperparameter grids, losses, LoRA, sampling, hardware, external assets, and the code/data repository link.

R1.justification: Related Work and all 41 references are unchanged, as is the positioning of HumorDB relative to prior textual, visual, and multimodal humor research.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v2 dated 24 Jul 2025 to v3 dated 17 Oct 2025, and PDF author metadata is corrected/reordered. Manuscript wording, displayed authors, and section structure are identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–14, Tables 1–6, captions, and page layouts are unchanged. Rendered pages match except for the updated first-page arXiv stamp.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, empirical evidence, supplementary analyses, explanations, and limitations are identical. Updating the version/date stamp and author metadata does not produce a meaningful overall difference in paper quality.
